response: It seems Cuba is heading into a political shakeup, but the real threat is how this will only deepen the already massive inequalities between the wealthy and everyone else. Ordinary people on the island have no resources and are far too broke to step in and take over the businesses that are still operating, leaving them shut out of any transition. Instead, the wealthy diaspora and foreign investors are positioned to swoop in and buy up property and assets for next to nothing. This isn't some neutral shift—it's a setup that hands even more power to the privileged elite while pushing vulnerable workers and communities further into the margins, entrenching structural exploitation rather than delivering any gains for those who've been left behind for so long. What we need is reform that actually centers labor rights and protects the most disadvantaged, not another round of dispossession that favors the few.
